{{multiple image|width=180|header=Overall Champions|image1= Hirscher-001.jpg|caption1=[[Marcel Hirscher]] won the overall title for the eighth successive year.|image2=Mikaela Shiffrin 2012 cropped.jpg|caption2=[[Mikaela Shiffrin]] won the overall title for the third successive year.|direction=horizontal}}
The [[International Ski Federation]] (FIS) '''Alpine Ski World Cup''' was the premier circuit for [[alpine skiing]] competition. The inaugural season launched in January [[1967 FIS Alpine Ski World Cup|1967]], and the {{nowrap|2018–19}} season marks the 53rd consecutive year for the [[International Ski Federation|FIS]] [[FIS Alpine Ski World Cup|World Cup]].

This season began in October 2018 in [[Sölden]], [[Austria]], and concluded in mid-March 2019 at the finals in [[Soldeu]], [[Andorra]]. The biennial [[FIS Alpine World Ski Championships 2019|World Championships]] interrupted the tour in early February in [[Åre ski resort|Åre]], [[Sweden]]. During the season, the most successful female skier of all time, four-time overall World Cup champion [[Lindsey Vonn]] of the United States, retired after the [[FIS Alpine World Ski Championships 2019|World Championships]], at which she won a bronze medal in downhill.  Also, two-time overall champion [[Aksel Lund Svindal]] of [[Norway]] retired at the same meet, at which he won a silver medal in downhill.<ref name="party">{{cite news |url=https://www.cdapress.com/article/20190203/AP/302039987 |first=Andrew |last=Dampf |title=RETIREMENT PARTY: Vonn and Svindal to Say Goodbye at Worlds |work=[[Coeur d'Alene Press]] |date=3 February 2019 |access-date=3 February 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190204231113/https://www.cdapress.com/article/20190203/AP/302039987 |archive-date=4 February 2019 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

[[Marcel Hirscher]] of Austria won his eighth straight men's overall championship, an all-time record, and moved in third place in overall wins (68) behind only Ingemar Stenmark (86) and Vonn (82).  [[Mikaela Shiffrin]] of the United States won her third straight women's overall championship and moved into 5th place on the overall win list (60).  After the season, Hirscher also retired.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://olympics.nbcsports.com/2019/09/04/marcel-hirscher-retire/| first=Nick |last=Zaccardi |title=Marcel Hirscher retires atop Alpine skiing rather than chase record |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=4 September 2019 |access-date=4 September 2019}}</ref>

==Women==
Prior to the start of the season, 4-time overall World Cup champion (and 20-time crystal globe winner) [[Lindsey Vonn]] of the [[United States]] announced her retirement effective as of the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://people.com/sports/lindsey-vonn-retiring-after-ski-season/ |first=Lindsay |last=Kimble |title=Lindsey Vonn to Retire After 2018-2019 Ski Season: 'It Has Been a Great Ride' |website=[[People (magazine)|People]] |date=October 12, 2018 |access-date=November 23, 2018}}</ref> Due to lingering injuries, she moved her retirement date up to the World Championships in February.<ref name="party" />

In December, Mikaela Shiffrin became the eighth athlete (four men, four women) to win [[FIS Alpine Ski World Cup#Most races won|at least 50 World Cup races across all disciplines]], as well as the youngest (at age 23) to do so.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/olympics/la-sp-skiiing-shiffrin-20181222-story.html |author=[[Associated Press]] |title=Mikaela Shiffrin continues to make World Cup history with 35th slalom win, her 50th overall |website=[[Los Angeles Times]]| date=22 January 2018 |access-date=22 January 2018}}</ref> Shiffrin ended the season with 17 race victories (3 Super Gs, 4 giant slaloms, 8 slaloms, and 2 parallel slaloms/city events), breaking [[Vreni Schneider]]'s 30-year-old record of 14 wins in a (much shorter) season, which was set in the [[1988–89 FIS Alpine Ski World Cup|1988-89 season]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2019/03/16/sport/mikaela-shiffrin-marcel-hirscher-skiing-world-cup-andorra-spt-intl/index.html |first=Rob |last=Hodgetts |title=Mikaela Shiffrin extends record run as Marcel Hirscher hints at retirement |work=[[CNN]] |date=March 16, 2019 |access-date=March 17, 2019}}</ref> Shiffrin also won four crystal globes for the season, tying the women's record held by Vonn and [[Tina Maze]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/shiffrin-leads-giant-slalom-set-4th-wcup-trophy-092925429.html |title=Shiffrin wins giant slalom race to seal World Cup title |work=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 17, 2019 |access-date=March 17, 2019}}</ref>

On 6 March 2019, former slalom season champion (and Olympic gold medalist) [[Frida Hansdotter]] announced her retirement from alpine skiing following the 2018–2019 season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.aftonbladet.se/sportbladet/a/jP6QQq/hansdotter-slutar-kanner-mig-klar|title=Hansdotter slutar|publisher=Sportbladet|language=sv|author=Ibraheem Alsalman|date=6 March 2019|access-date=6 March 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.gp.se/sport/frida-hansdotter-avslutar-karri%C3%A4ren-1.13853817|title=Frida Hansdotter avslutar karriären|publisher=Göteborgsposten|language=sv|author=Jonatan Andersson|date=6 March 2019|access-date=6 March 2019}}</ref>
